messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv-cache metadata growth detected in paged-blockmgr cluster us-west-2. Tail request latency > 95th for customer 'AcmePay' over the last 3m. Auto-throttle triggered on canary pool.

DeployBot: deploy started: rollback-slowpath-hotfix -> canary (5 nodes). Triggered by @Maya L per runbook.

Maya L: saw a sharp bump in 'meta_size_bytes' for blocks >= 128KB, looks like metadata headers accumulating and preventing eviction. tail latency correlated with continuous-batching spikes.

Devin P: assigning oncall. I'll take lead. Initial impact: 3 customer endpoints reporting p95 > 1200ms, some 5xx spike (rate ~0.3%). Not widespread yet.

Sasha R: adding context — last night we pushed batch-config v2 that increases max_inflight to 48 and reduces batch flush threshold to 8ms for throughput. I suspect that lowered eviction opportunities and allowed many small KV writes to create a metadata fanout.

Tina C: @Devin can you run the quick-check script and post the top offending block IDs? Command: ```/ops/check-kv-meta --cluster us-west-2 --top 20```

Devin P: running now... attaching output excerpt below (sanitized):
```
top_meta_growth:
 - block_id: b-7f3a, meta_bytes: 182394, last_touch: 2026-03-15T09:12:03Z
 - block_id: b-12c4, meta_bytes: 171102, last_touch: 2026-03-15T09:11:58Z
 - block_id: b-94ab, meta_bytes: 169800, last_touch: 2026-03-15T09:12:10Z
```

Devin P: blocks are large, metadata is ~170KB each, > expected header size. Looks like repeated partial writes created many small entries.

Samir G: propose immediate mitigations: 1) reduce continuous-batching inflight to 24 on canary, 2) enable metadata-compact on canary (non-disruptive), 3) temporary canary-level eviction aggressiveness + decrease block size ceiling to 96KB. We can do 1+2 now.

Maya L: agreed. Samir, can you push the config delta for the canary pool? Example patch: ```yaml
# canary runtime overrides
continuous_batching:
  max_inflight: 24
  flush_threshold_ms: 12
block_manager:
  block_size_max: 98304  # 96KB
  metadata_compact: true
```

Samir G: pushing override to canary now. `kubectl apply -f canary-runtime-override.yaml` -> success. DeployBot: canary config applied.

DeployBot: live traffic routing adjusted: canary receive 8% of traffic for AcmePay endpoints. Monitoring: 95th latency and meta_size trend.

Tina C: monitoring graphs show meta_size slope decreasing on canary after config change. p95 improved from ~1300ms -> ~420ms on canary within 90s.

Devin P: good. Next: plan for cluster-wide rollout or alternate fallback? Risk: compaction may stall other components. I recommend staged rollout with 30m observation window, and prepare rollback plan to previous batch-config.

Maya L: agree. Also need customer-facing note: low severity performance degradation; we mitigated via canary config and are rolling a staged fix. @Sasha can you draft a short message for Customer Ops?

Sasha R: drafting: "We observed a performance spike affecting a subset of requests. We've applied a targeted canary config that reduced the impact. We're rolling the fix cluster-wide after verification. No data loss. ETA for full rollout ~45-60m." Will post in #customer-ops after approvals.

Samir G: starting cluster-wide rollout to remaining pools with 10% rollout steps every 6 minutes. Watchers: @Devin @Maya @Tina. If p95 regresses >15% we abort.

Devin P: abort condition triggered in eu-west-1 at step 2 (p95 regressed 18%). Rolling back eu-west-1 to previous config and pausing rollout. Investigating difference in block fragmentation patterns between regions.

Maya L: capture logs for discrepancy: run `curl -s http://internal-metrics/eu-west-1/blockmgr/frag | jq '.'` and paste top histogram.

Tina C: eu-west fragment histogram shows many small fragments <4KB but higher count vs us-west. That means different workload; lowering block_size_max may not help there. We're switching eu-west to metadata_compact=true + reduce flush_threshold_ms to 6ms instead of decreasing block_size_max.

Sasha R: customer ops update ready, posting now. @CustomerOps please tag any impacted users and reference incident id: 2026-03-15-kv-meta-02.

Devin P: postmortem notes for follow-up: 1) revert batch-config v2 default change or add safety (per-cluster heuristics), 2) add automated detection for meta_size per-block > 64KB spike alerts, 3) add runbook step for region-specific rollout with fragmentation check.

Maya L: also file an SRE ticket to audit writes that create high metadata churn (probably partial-key updates). I'll start a trace-based sampling job for affected endpoints.

Samir G: changing incident severity to SEV3 -> monitoring until stable. I'll remain oncall for next 60m.

Devin P: thanks everyone. I'll close thread when eu-west stabilization confirmed. :thumbsup:
